thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Mixed Even As Dow Surges to Record High

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Mixed Even As Dow Surges to Record High
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Tuesday's regular session:
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): +2.6%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ):-0.9%
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): +5.8%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.3%
iShares China Large-Cap ETF ( FXI ): -2%
SPDR S&P 500 (SPY): +0.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were mixed. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 0.2%.
US stocks were mixed at session's half, with gains sparked by component stock Intel (INTC), which propelled the Dow Jones Industrial Average to set another all-time high. The S&P 500 is also off its sessions lows and trading in positive territory, while Nasdaq slipped lower.
Earlier, concerns about the fallout from Italy's 2019 budget weighed on European equities and left investors searching for safe havens, causing further deterioration of Monday's USMCA-fueled rally.
The Dow circled the flatline at the open before racing higher thanks to a sharp rebound in Intel, gaining as much as 5% to set a two-month high. The semiconductor stock was under pressure Monday when analysts cautioned that its battle with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) could become very costly.
The Dow's move higher is also being amplified by strength in the industrial sector with shares of component stock Boeing (BA) at its third straight record high. Apple (AAPL), Caterpillar (CAT) and Walgreen (WBA) are also contributing to a triple-digit gain in the blue chip index.
The upbeat price action in the US failed to underpin European bourses with all the major indices trading lower. The showdown between the new government in Rome with the European Union prompted Goldman Sachs to warn that "contagion risks have risen" as Italy's bloated budget deficit could raise risks for an exit from the EU. Tuesday's losses were largely to blame on comments from Lega party member and Euro-skeptic Claudio Borghi calling for Italy to adopt its own currency.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.7% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were higher.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.3% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were weaker.
Level Brands, Inc. (LEVB) rose nearly 13% after it said it closed an underwritten public offering for total gross proceeds of about $6.9 million. Shares jumped more than 10.3% intraday. The company sold 1,971,428 shares at $3.50 each in this offering, which included the full exercise of the over-allotment option of 257,142 shares. The company said it intends to use the net proceeds for brand development and expansion, acquisitions and general working capital.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.3%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 0.7% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 0.6%.
Bank of Nova Scotia (BNS) fell more than 1% after it said it has been fined $800,000 by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for "engaging in multiple acts of spoofing in gold and silver futures contracts traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange," according to the CFTC Web site. The bank will also be required to implement measures to detect and deter spoofing. The CFTC determined the bank engaged in the activity from "at least June 2013" through June 2016. The bank was notified of the misconduct by its Futures Commission Merchant and reported it to the CFTC.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 0.3% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were in the green.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 0.6% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.7%.
Atomera (ATOM) jumped nearly 12% after it unveiled a license deal with STMicroelectronics (STM), giving the latter certain rights to integrate Atomera's Mears Silicon Technology or MST into its products. MST is a patented material that can improve transistors' performance in electronics such as mobile phones and the companies' license deal is the first stage of a three-phase licensing process, with manufacturing and distribution as the next two phases. STM shares rose more than 2%.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.2% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.3%.
CenterPoint Energy (CNP) rose marginally after the company said its competitive natural gas sales and services business, CenterPoint Energy Services, has expanded its retail natural gas supply to residential customers and businesses of all sizes in Illinois. The company said that its expansion of services, which began this month, builds on its established presence in Illinois where it currently serves more than 6,000 commercial and industrial customers.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.4%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.6%. Natural gas was up 2.9% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 2.5%.
Gold was up 1.3%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 1.1%. Silver was down 1.5%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 1.3%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 0.7%.
Clovis Oncology (CLVS) jumped 12% after the company said that the US Food and Drug Administration has granted a second breakthrough therapy designation for Rubraca. The monotherapy treatment is for adult patients with BRCA1/2-mutated mCRPC who have received at least one prior androgen receptor (AR)-directed therapy and taxane-based chemotherapy. This designation was granted to Rubraca based on initial efficacy and safety results from TRITON2, the phase 2 study in men with advanced prostate cancer with BRCA 1/2 mutations (germline or somatic) and deleterious mutations of other homologous recombination (HR) repair genes, in the metastatic castration-resistant setting. Initial data from the study, which served as the basis for designation, will be presented for the first time at the 2018 European Society for Medical Oncology Congress, which is scheduled to be held Oct. 19-23 in Munich, Germany.
